title: Trade access, but let students steer the fee bargain
answer: In this simulation, Britain should accept shared food and carbon rules for easier trade, but offer home fees only with equal terms for UK students abroad. Fee talks are still open (s4). Parliament should set that bargain. Elected student and staff boards at each university should check its costs. Employers wanting to recruit through the youth scheme should fund any fee gap through a charge for taking part. No signed funding, no fee concession. Publish the accounts each year. Judge success by cheaper food, shorter border waits, students travelling both ways, falling emissions and no lost university places or courses.
